2026-11-19.title: Third Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Bearing fruit in every good work
The seed on good soil bears fruit
2026-11-19.verse: But as for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit.
theo: Paul thanks God that the Gospel “is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world,” and prays that the Colossians may “lead lives worthy of the Lord… bearing fruit in every good work.” The Church is God's field.

Jesus explains the sower: the same seed falls on the path, rocky ground, thorns and good soil. The difference lies in the hearing. “Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.” Good soil is a heart that hears, understands and keeps the word, and so bears fruit thirty, sixty and a hundredfold.
outline: Ask: what kind of soil was your heart this week?
Point 1 · The word is bearing fruit
The Gospel grows in the whole world.
Hardness, shallowness and worries choke the word.
live: Name one worry or distraction and give it to God.
Read tomorrow's Gospel the night before.
2026-11-19.prayer: Lord, sow your word in my heart. Break up its hardness, deepen its soil, pull out the thorns, and make it bear fruit in every good work. Amen.

quick: The Gospel is bearing fruit in the whole world.
The difference is in the hearing.
Good soil hears, understands and bears fruit.

2026-11-19.question: What chokes the word in my heart?

homily: Dear friends, Paul thanks God that the Gospel is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world, and prays that the Colossians may lead lives worthy of the Lord, bearing fruit in every good work (Colossians 1:6, 10). The Church is God's field.

Jesus explains the parable of the sower: the same seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil. The one who hears the word and understands it bears fruit, a hundredfold, sixtyfold, thirtyfold (Matthew 13:18–23). The difference is not in the seed but in the soil.

What kind of soil is my heart today? A path trodden hard by hurry, shallow rock, or thorns of worry? Let us pull out one thorn this week: one hour less on the phone, one hour more with the Word. Amen.
kids: Children, God's word is like a seed. Listen carefully so you can be good soil! Tell your family one word you heard in church today.

intro: The Gospel grows in the world; the sower's seed bears fruit in hearts that hear.

points.h: The word does not return empty
sub: God's word always accomplishes its purpose.
The Gospel is bearing fruit worldwide.
q: So shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
points.apply: Thank God for those who sowed the word in you.

sub: Isaiah warned of ears that hear but do not understand.
Hardness and worry choke the seed.
q: Keep listening, but do not comprehend; keep looking, but do not understand.
As for what was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the lure of wealth choke the word, and it yields nothing.
points.apply: Name one worry and give it to God.

sub: Good soil hears, understands and keeps.
Fruit is seen in good works.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season.
But as for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty.

concl: The seed is good; let the soil be good.
Blessed are the ears that hear.
2026-11-19.resolve: Give ten minutes to the word of God every day this week.
